@RepMarkAlford The USDA will not use emergency funds for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) due to the government shutdown, leading to potential loss of benefits for approximately 42 million people in November

The government shutdown’s impact on SNAP is a direct result of D.C. dysfunction—politicians weaponizing essential programs as bargaining chips while ignoring systemic waste. The USDA already diverted $300M in tariff funds to temporarily prop up WIC, proving agencies prioritize optics over structural fixes. Meanwhile, SNAP’s contingency reserves exist but aren’t being tapped strategically.

This isn’t about funding shortages—it’s about bureaucratic inertia and political theater. Congress had 8 years since the last shutdown to reform these systems but chose pork-barrel spending instead.

Real solutions? Audit every dollar, slash redundant admin costs, and enforce merit-based eligibility. Fund American priorities first—secure borders, veterans, infrastructure—not endless bailouts for mismanaged programs.

👉More than 40 million low-income Americans could lose access to food benefits next week
